question: What is the main thing that makes cancer cells different from normal body cells?

options.A: Growing and spreading without normal body control
options.B: Destroying tissues only when bacteria are present

explanation: Think of normal cells as following strict traffic rules, while cancer cells throw out the rulebook and multiply uncontrollably. You've got this!

question: Why is it super important for nurses in primary health clinics to know about cancer?

options.A: Primary health centers run all national chemotherapy programs
options.B: Infectious diseases are no longer treated in Nigeria
options.C: Community clinics handle complex surgeries daily
options.D: Nurses are usually the first health workers patients see with early symptoms

explanation: Spotting early signs at the grass-roots level means we can refer patients quickly and save lives. Great nursing starts in the community!

question: What do we call the process when cancer cells break away and travel to other parts of the body?
explanation: Metastasis is just the medical term for cancer packing its bags and traveling through the blood or lymph to start a new tumor elsewhere. You're mastering the terms!

question: What actually happens during the 'promotion' stage of cancer development?

options.A: Mutated cells are stimulated to divide over and over
options.B: Cancer cells immediately travel to the brain
options.C: All abnormal cells safely destroy themselves
options.D: Normal DNA is completely repaired by enzymes

explanation: During promotion, things like lifestyle factors or irritants encourage those already-changed cells to keep multiplying into a bigger problem.

question: Which common virus is strongly linked to the development of cervical cancer?
explanation: High-risk strains of HPV can cause changes in cervical cells over time. This is why screening and the HPV vaccine are such big wins in public health!

question: A 45-year-old woman comes to the clinic with a hard, painless breast lump she noticed six months ago. What often causes this kind of late presentation in our communities?

options.A: Cultural stigma and trying alternative therapies first
options.D: The tumor was already surgically removed

explanation: Fear, stigma, and trying traditional remedies first are real barriers our patients face. As nurses, part of our job is compassionate, judgment-free education.

question: Which viral infection is a major risk factor for liver cancer?
explanation: Chronic Hepatitis B causes long-term inflammation and scarring in the liver, which can eventually lead to liver cancer. Vaccination is key!

question: Why is smoking tobacco such a major risk factor for many types of cancer?

options.A: It introduces living cancer cells into the lungs
options.B: It blocks all major blood vessels
options.C: It contains harmful chemicals that damage cellular DNA
options.D: It stops red blood cells from forming

explanation: Tobacco smoke has active chemical carcinogens that mess up the genetic code inside healthy cells, triggering abnormal growth.

question: During a Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA) screening for cervical pre-cancer, what liquid is applied to the cervix?
explanation: Acetic acid is simply the active ingredient in vinegar! It makes abnormal cells temporarily turn white so the nurse can spot them easily.

question: What is the main purpose of cancer screening programs in primary health care?

options.A: To find out the patient's family tree
options.B: To completely replace laboratory blood tests
options.D: To catch abnormalities before symptoms and spreading happen

explanation: Screening is all about catching issues early when treatment is easiest and most successful. Prevention is better than cure!

question: In the famous 'CAUTION' warning signs of cancer, what does the letter 'U' stand for?
explanation: Remember CAUTION! The 'U' reminds us to never ignore unexplained bleeding or discharge from any part of the body. Keep that in your nursing toolkit!

question: A patient has had a hoarse voice and a nagging cough for over three months that won't go away with antibiotics. Which cancer warning sign does this match?
explanation: That's the 'N' in CAUTION: a nagging cough or hoarseness. When a symptom sticks around way too long, it's time for a deeper check-up!

question: How should pain medication be given for chronic cancer pain according to standard guidelines?

options.A: Only when the pain becomes unbearable
options.B: Only when the patient remembers to ask
options.C: On a regular schedule around the clock
options.D: Strictly as a single bedtime dose

explanation: Scheduled dosing keeps the pain under control smoothly, rather than waiting for it to spike and trying to chase it down. Smart nursing care!

question: Why do many advanced cancer patients experience severe weight loss and muscle wasting?

options.A: Permanent blockage of the large intestine only
options.B: A total loss of the brain's thirst center
options.C: Being forced to do too much heavy exercise
options.D: Metabolic changes caused by the tumor and treatments

explanation: Cancer changes how the body uses energy, leading to a condition called cachexia where muscle and fat break down fast. Nutritional support is so vital here.

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care?

options.A: To speed up the dying process
options.C: To improve quality of life and relieve suffering

explanation: Palliative care is all about comfort, dignity, and making sure patients and their families feel supported when a cure isn't possible. Beautiful, compassionate nursing!

question: Why is community health education so crucial for fighting cancer in Nigeria?

options.A: It replaces the need for palliative nurses
options.B: It guarantees free surgeries at every health post
options.C: It helps clear up harmful myths and encourages early hospital visits
options.D: It completely stops genetic mutations from happening

explanation: When we educate our communities with love and facts, we break down fear and cultural barriers so people seek help early. You are going to make a great nurse!
